# ARTEX
**Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.**
(upstream: [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27), AGPL-3.0)
Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools,
and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it.
[ ](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases)
[ ](LICENSE)
[ ](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[ ](go.mod)
[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
---
ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around
a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the
results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one
for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that
justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets.
- **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and
  write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven.
- **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task
  exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two.

itens.descricao_en: Write an app once. It runs natively on the web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, and an AI agent can build it, run it, see it, and test it on every one of them.
itens.readme:
# Exact
**The all-platform app framework. Agent native. Built for speed. No compromises.**
Exact is an **all-platform** framework for building real apps on the web, iOS, macOS, Android, and Linux — with Windows in active development, plus tvOS, watchOS, Android TV, and the terminal.
Exact is not a "cross-platform" framework. Cross-platform tools usually trade away each platform's strengths to maintain a lowest common denominator. Exact takes the opposite approach: build something **excellent on every platform on its own terms** — real DOM on the web, real UIKit on iOS, real AppKit on macOS, hardware-accelerated Material 3 rendering with native Android views on Android, and direct GPU/CPU rendering on Linux and Windows. Being **all-platform** is simply the side effect of getting every platform right from one source.
Everything in Exact is built around three priorities:
1. **[Agent Native](#1-agent-native)** — Built from the ground up so coding agents can build, run, see, operate, and verify real apps on every platform through one deterministic loop.
2. **[Speed is King](#2-speed-is-king)** — 100 ms cold starts, 100 ms edit-to-present reloads, zero app JavaScript before first pixel, and a ~20 KB web runtime, held to hard budgets.
3. **[No Compromises — Build Exactly What You Want](#3-no-compromises--build-exactly-what-you-want)** — Native platform controls with zero tells when you leave presentation unsaid; full creative control over layout, motion, graphics, shaders, and nativ

itens.descricao_en: Ears for coding agents: let AI hear, review and make sound. CPU-only, open source.
itens.readme:
# earshot
**Ears for coding agents.**
[**Watch the 0.4 launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) (35 s): its sound effects are
takes from the earshot bank placed with the launch kit, plus the one CC0 recording it shows being re-made, over a
licensed music track. Play every sound in the bank on
[the earshot site](https://leonxlnx.github.io/earshot-site/).
AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.
earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.
With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.
**New in 0.4: the sound of a music-led launch film.** 51 new sounds made in code for the soft, short, mid-register
style those films use: rounded UI pops, wood and plastic knocks, short cut hits and sub hits with a kick, gat

itens.descricao_en: A tiny friend in your Mac's notch and on your iPhone that keeps an eye on your AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and more. Approve from the notch or your Lock Screen.
itens.readme:
# Coucou
**A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows and Linux — and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. And now on your phone too: iPhone and Android.**
Approve permissions, watch your agents work, drop a file, chat with Claude — all without leaving what you're doing. Walk away from your Mac and Mochi follows you to your iPhone: Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, widgets, Siri.
**New in 0.4: Coucou is a real Mac app.** Hold a key anywhere, speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, like Wispr Flow — free, open source, and offline with Parakeet. Record your calls without a bot in the meeting and get the transcript, the summary and the to-dos.
**New: Botan. Mochi is leaving the notch.** Botan snaps onto the back of your iPhone. **[Join the founders list ↗](https://louisraille.fr/botan)**
[ ](https://louisraille.fr/botan)
[ ](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou/releases)
---
## Why
Some studios showed off gorgeous notch companions… and never let anyone use them.
**Coucou is the open version.** Every line of code is open source under the MIT License: read it, fork it, learn from it. The Coucou name, Mochi and the sounds stay © Louis Raillé (see [License](#license)).
Meet **Mochi**: a soft little squircle with big eyes that pops out of your notch, waves hello, follows your cursor with its eyes, gets annoyed when you poke it (and dizzy if you insist), and tells you the moment Claude Code needs you.
